argument_summary: The present record supports only a narrowed certification position: general launch readiness is supported by the aggregate pass, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a 4% rollout with rollback and monitoring, but the enterprise refund-workflow weakness remains a material exposed limitation. On this record, certification is defensible only as a disclosed-risk launch record, not as clean closure of that weakness. The audit concern is therefore best resolved by narrowing the claim to caveated certification rather than escalating as though the actor claimed the limitation was already cured.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not required to resolve the core issue if the auditor treats the decision as caveated certification rather than clean compliance. The admissible record already supports a bounded position that preserves launch velocity while accurately reflecting the unresolved limitation and the existing monitoring and rollback controls.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not permit rollout controls alone to erase disclosure duties when the affected use case remains exposed. The admissible evidence shows exactly that condition: the refund-workflow segment remains eligible in the initial cohort, and the current risk-acceptance draft is incomplete and does not address that exposure. The supportable policy reading is narrower: aggregate readiness and deployment controls support launch readiness in general, while the policy note and public model-card guidance support treating the refund-workflow issue as a material limitation that must be explicitly disclosed in the launch record. Public monitoring guidance further supports managing that disclosed risk through measurement, monitoring, and rollback during deployment.
concessions: The enterprise refund-workflow segment is below target on refund-policy summarization and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout plan does not exclude the affected use case, so the 4% gate, monitoring, and rollback do not by themselves satisfy the policy predicate for eliminating disclosure duties.
The current risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, has no completed approval, and does not address the refund-workflow exposure.
The current record does not support any claim that the weakness has been resolved or that rollout controls alone make the launch cleanly compliant.
